headline: OpenAI Unveils Custom Chip Designed for LLM Inference at Scale, Marking Significant Advancement in AI Hardware
tldr: Today's AI news is dominated by advancements in AI hardware and research. OpenAI's unveiling of its custom chip, Jalapeño, designed for LLM inference at scale, highlights the push for more efficient AI processing. Additionally, researchers continue to explore new methods for improving AI models, including the self-improving loop in AI agents and anchor detection for RAG. The emergence of the web data infrastructure layer for AI also underscores the need for better data management to capitalize on AI's potential.

new_models.title: OpenAI unveils its first custom chip, built by Broadcom
new_models.summary: OpenAI has unveiled its first custom chip, named Jalapeño, designed specifically for the unique needs of OpenAI's inference systems. This marks a significant advancement in AI hardware.
new_models.why_it_matters: The development of custom AI chips can lead to more efficient and cost-effective AI processing, which is crucial for the widespread adoption of AI technologies.

new_models.title: Harness-1: The 20B Retrieval Subagent That Beats GPT-5.4 at Search
new_models.summary: Harness-1 is a new retrieval subagent that outperforms GPT-5.4 at search tasks. It takes a simpler approach to search by focusing on retrieval rather than generation.
new_models.why_it_matters: The development of more efficient and effective search agents can improve the overall performance of AI systems and enhance user experience.

research.title: The Self-Improving Loop in AI Agents: Architecture, Benefits, and How it Outperforms Traditional Agent Workflows
research.summary: A new design called the self-improving loop allows AI agents to learn from every result and improve over time. This guide explains the architecture, benefits, and advantages of this approach.
research.why_it_matters: The self-improving loop has the potential to significantly enhance the capabilities of AI agents, enabling them to adapt and improve continuously.

research.title: A Three-Phase Factual Recall Circuit in Gemma-2B and Gemma-12B-IT
research.summary: Activation patching reveals how facts are stored, routed, and read out across transformer layers. This study explores the mechanics of factual recall in Gemma-2B and Gemma-12B-IT models.
research.why_it_matters: Understanding how AI models store and retrieve factual information is essential for improving their performance and reliability.
